notes:
I couldn't write any notes on Jonah 2 this time. The research tools stopped working before any page loaded. My first batch of page requests hit the tool's usage limit, and when I tried a smaller batch I was told I had no tool calls left for this turn. So I haven't read a single source.

You asked me to report only what the pages actually say, with a URL for each point. Without any pages read, anything I wrote would come from my own memory, so I've left it all out.

When the tools are available again, I plan to read these pages in this order:

1. **Verse-by-verse (traditional reading):**
   - Enduring Word, Jonah 2: https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/jonah-2/
   - Precept Austin, Jonah 2: https://www.preceptaustin.org/jonah-2-commentary
   - Bible Hub: Ellicott, Gill, Pulpit Commentary and Matthew Henry on Jonah 2 (biblehub.com/commentaries/…/jonah/2.htm)
   - StudyLight: Wesley's Notes (Methodist) on Jonah 2
2. **Where Protestant traditions differ:** Spurgeon's sermons on v. 9 ("Salvation is from the LORD"), plus Ligonier, Desiring God, GTY, Seedbed, 1517 and LCMS pages on Jonah 2. These should show how each tradition reads vv. 8–9 and the Jonah-and-Christ link in v. 10.
3. **Other views:**
   - NET Bible notes on "Sheol" (v. 2), the temple (vv. 4, 7) and whether the psalm was part of the book from the start: https://netbible.org/bible/Jonah+2
   - Bible Odyssey on Jonah
   - Catholic and Orthodox readings: New Advent's Church Fathers (Jerome, Augustine on Jonah as a sign of Christ) and OCA

Try sending the request again, or ask for one or two verses at a time to keep the number of tool calls down. Then I'll write the notes verse by verse with a URL for every point.
